medications.purpose: Blood pressure control and potential disease‑modifying therapy for HFrEF
medications.nice_justification: NG106 first‑line ACE‑inhibitor for HFrEF; dose reduced because of low BP (104/58 mmHg) and eGFR 57.8 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.purpose: Avoid additive hypotension and volume depletion in an elderly patient with low BP and CKD
medications.nice_justification: Not required for HF without congestion; NICE advises against unnecessary diuretics when BP is already low

medications.medication: Insulin isophane (glargine) 70 U/mL and regular insulin 30 U/mL
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control for diabetes; current HbA1c 3.2 % indicates overtreatment
medications.nice_justification: Diabetes management per NICE; dose reduction required to prevent hypoglycaemia

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive hypotensive effect and risk of electrolyte disturbance (hyponatraemia, hypokalaemia)
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue hydrochlorothiazide; monitor BP and electrolytes after ACE‑I dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: Improved renal perfusion and lower BP may increase insulin sensitivity, raising hypoglycaemia risk
interactions_checked.action: Review and reduce insulin dose; advise frequent glucose monitoring

assumptions_warnings: LVEF not documented – cannot confirm HFrEF; disease‑modifying HF drugs (beta‑blocker, MRA, SGLT2‑i) are deferred until echocardiogram is performed.
Serum potassium not available – MRA cannot be started safely.
No record of NYHA class or congestion – loop diuretic not indicated at present.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I angio‑edema before dose change.
QRISK/ cardiovascular risk score not provided – cannot assess need for primary‑prevention statin.
treatment_summary: The patient is already on lisinopril 10 mg, which is a NICE‑recommended ACE‑inhibitor for HF, but the dose is too high for her low blood pressure and stage 3a CKD; it has been reduced to 5 mg daily. Hydrochlorothiazide is stopped to avoid further hypotension and electrolyte imbalance. Insulin therapy is continued but flagged for urgent dose reduction because HbA1c 3.2 % indicates overtreatment. No beta‑blocker, MRA, SGLT2‑inhibitor or loop diuretic is started until echocardiography, potassium, and congestion status are clarified. Monitoring includes BP, renal function, electrolytes, and glucose after any medication change, and referral for cardiac imaging and diabetes review.
